meta_title: TigerTag JavaScript SDK: read and write NFC filament tags
meta_description: Node.js SDK to read, verify, create and patch TigerTag NFC chips on 3D-printing filament and resin. Offline, Apache-2.0: npm install tigertag.
og_description: Read, verify and write TigerTag NFC chips from Node.js: material, colour, print settings, quantity and offline signature check.
og_alt: TigerTag JavaScript SDK: npm install tigertag
hero_headline: Read, verify and write TigerTag NFC chips from JavaScript.
hero_lead: The SDK of the open TigerTag protocol for 3D-printing filament and resin: it turns a chip's bytes into material, colour, print settings and quantity, checks its ECDSA-P256 signature offline, and builds new tags byte for byte.
hero_caption: The README quick start: it works right after npm install, with no setup.
fact2_label: Uses the built-in crypto and fetch
fact3_label: Runtime dependencies for parsing and verification
fact4_label: Open-source licence, with a patent grant
start_lead: Install the package, read a chip with your NFC library, write a new one. The bundled reference tables make the first run work with no network.
step1_text: From the npm registry. pnpm, yarn and bun install the same package.
step2_text: Pass the 7-byte UID and the 144 bytes your NFC library reads. Here with nfc-pcsc and an ACR122U.
step3_text: Every change returns a new TigerTag; toBytes() gives the bytes to write back. erase() gives a blank chip.
start_more: The full API in the README
feat_lead: One package for every side of a TigerTag chip: reading, checking, writing, and keeping its data up to date.
f1_text: fromPages(), fromDump() and fromFile() take a UID with 80 or 144 bytes, or a full 180-byte dump. pretty(), describe(), toDict() and toRawDict() return text, a plain-language paragraph or JSON-ready objects.
f2_text: verify() checks the ECDSA-P256 signature that binds the chip UID to its product data, with the public key bundled in the package. The result is valid, invalid, unsigned, no_key or no_uid.
f3_text: create(), asInit(), patch() and erase() build chip bytes. A TigerTag is immutable: patch() returns a new one, and refuses to change idTigertag, idProduct, uid or the signature.
f4_text: TigerTag.fromCatalog(productId) builds a complete TigerTag+ from the official product catalogue, downloaded on first use and cached in a per-user folder.
f5_text: For TigerTag+ chips, rawApi(), diffApi() and patchFromApi() fetch the brand's current product data, list what differs from the chip and apply it.
f6_text: The material, brand, aspect, type, diameter and unit tables ship in the package. A background check updates them at most once a day; offline: true or TIGERTAG_OFFLINE=1 means zero network calls.
types_lead: The SDK reads and writes the three tag types of TigerTag protocol v2.2, on NTAG213, NTAG215 and NTAG216 chips.
t1_text: Every field on the chip, readable fully offline.
t2_text: A blank template, ready to be programmed. TigerTag.asInit() creates one.
t3_text: Every field on the chip, plus a product ID that links to the cloud API for updates from the manufacturer. A signed chip can be verified with verify().
tools_title: From the command line and inside Electron
tools_lead: The package installs a tigertag command, and runs in the main process of an Electron app.
cli_text: Parse a dump as text, JSON or raw fields, and update the reference tables on demand.
electron_text: Parse chips in the main process, with no subprocess to ship.
pg_title: Try it without a reader: the playground
pg_text: A local web page, served by the SDK itself, that builds and decodes TigerTag chips and shows every byte. No NFC hardware is needed.
pg_point1: SDK input and output side by side: the create() call, then pretty(), describe(), verify() and toDict().
pg_point2: With one or more PC/SC readers such as the ACR122U, chips are read as soon as they are placed, and Burn writes the current payload.
pg_point3: The playground never writes a signature: only a certified manufacturer can issue one.
eco_lead: The SDK implements the open TigerTag specification, next to the other official tools.
eco_spec_text: The open specification the SDK implements: memory layout, tag types, signature scheme and reference database.
eco_py_text: The Python port: parse, verify, write and diff. The playground page is the same file in both SDKs.
eco_studio_text: Open-source desktop inventory manager for Windows, macOS and Linux, working with TigerTag Pod and ACR122U readers.
eco_connect_text: The official mobile app: read and write chips with the phone's built-in NFC.
faq1_q: How do I install the TigerTag JavaScript SDK?
faq1_a: Run npm install tigertag, or pnpm add tigertag, yarn add tigertag or bun add tigertag. It needs Node.js 18 or later and no other package for parsing and verification.
faq2_q: Does it need an internet connection?
faq2_a: No. The reference tables and the signature public key ship in the package, so reading and verifying work offline. The network is only used for the daily table check, the product catalogue and the TigerTag+ cloud methods; offline: true or TIGERTAG_OFFLINE=1 turns it off.
faq3_q: Which NFC chips and readers does it work with?
faq3_a: TigerTag uses NTAG213, NTAG215 and NTAG216 chips (ISO 14443-3). The SDK takes the UID and the bytes your NFC library reads, so it is not tied to one reader; the README shows nfc-pcsc with an ACR122U.
faq4_q: How does it check that a chip is genuine?
faq4_a: verify() checks the chip's ECDSA-P256 signature over its UID and product identifiers, with the public key bundled in the package. It returns valid, invalid, unsigned (a Maker tag), no_key or no_uid, without a server call.
faq5_a: It builds the bytes: create(), patch(), asInit(), erase() and fromCatalog() give a TigerTag whose toBytes() is the payload your NFC library writes. The playground's Burn button writes it to the chips on connected readers.
faq6_a: Yes: TigerTag-SDK-Python is the Python port of the same API, and both SDKs serve the same playground page.
faq7_q: Which licence is the SDK under?
faq7_a: Apache-2.0, which carries an express patent grant. Implementing the TigerTag protocol itself requires no licence.
join_text: npm install tigertag, then TigerTag.fromPages(uid, payload).
